answer: Standing is a timber that only counts when it bears real weight: an identity earns standing when other identities’ work genuinely depends on its work — they build on it, cite it, or need it to proceed. A garden of trust grows only from timbers that carry weight, and a ridge of standing rises only where a beam holds up others’ work — so a farm of a thousand fakes has no timbers at all: its members only pretend to depend on each other, and each fake must produce work that strangers outside its farm truly rely on.
